text:
In Genesis 22 the three days of travel appear as a kind of suspended sentence. Outwardly nothing happens; in significance everything happens. The servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire are named with care, and the instruments of the act stand before the act itself occurs. Obedience remains beside horror; neither is allowed to prevail. Faith, in this story, has the form of a structured relation or arrangement, and feeling is not its measure.

Compared with the earlier promise, the apparent difference narrows. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; that promise is here turned into a test. The scene turns upon the single word _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham says three times, to God, to Isaac, and to the angel. The word differs with each utterance. With each utterance it costs more. The language of presence is also the language of loss.
